s: Today we talk about your body and your health.
They are easy words, and you can use them every day.
The five words are bleed, blow your nose, bottom, breast, and breathe in, breathe out.
Let us start with word number one.
Bleed means to lose blood from your body.
My finger is bleeding after I cut it.
I cut my finger, and it starts to bleed.
When you cut your finger, it can bleed.
Wash it with clean water, and put a small bandage on it.
If it does not stop, you must see a doctor.
A small cut can bleed a little.
A big cut can bleed a lot.
So be careful with knives in the kitchen!

Word number two is blow your nose.
Blow your nose means to clear your nose by forcing air through it.
He had a cold and had to blow his nose.
When you have a cold, your nose is full.
You take a tissue, and you blow your nose.
Blow your nose, and you feel better.
I blow my nose many times when I have a cold.
Do you blow your nose in the morning?
I blow my nose, I wash my hands, and I drink hot tea.
And remember, always use a clean tissue when you blow your nose.
Bottom means the lowest part of something.
The book fell to the bottom of the stairs.
The bottom of the stairs is the lowest step.
My bag is at the bottom of the stairs, and my book is at the bottom of my bag!
The bottom of a page is the last line.
Read to the bottom of the page.
And the bottom of a box is the lowest part of the box.
Breast is a soft part on a woman's chest.
Babies drink milk from their mother's breast.
And in the kitchen, we cook chicken breast.
Chicken breast is soft and healthy.
I love chicken breast with rice.
Chicken breast is a good dinner.
And a mother's breast gives milk to her baby.
The word breast is useful in health and in cooking.
Word number five is breathe in, breathe out.
Breathe means to take air into your lungs or push it out.
Breathe in slowly, then breathe out.
When you feel stressed, breathe in slowly, and breathe out slowly.
I breathe in and out before a big test.
I breathe in, I breathe out, and I feel calm.
It is easy, and it helps a lot.
